status: assigned implementation contracts; not runtime admission or executable coverage

common.ownership: Isolate-owned state and terms; preserve native representations, moving roots and code leases. No host-global mutable substitutes.
common.accounting: Bounded entry charge plus causal traversal/construction/cleanup work; temporary and retained storage are accounted. Prepare before publication; preserve the first failure cause.
common.errors: Native guest errors for supported cases; explicit uncatchable host capability failure for reviewed unavailable modes. Resource/OOM/cancellation remain distinct.
common.invocation_paths: Direct exported and dynamic calls for every MFA; review compiler lowering, guard/body and intrinsic paths separately. BEAM wrappers retain necessary exact-name dependencies.
common.tests: Independent native reference cases, malformed/boundary inputs, lowered/dynamic calls, GC and code retention, memory/work/allocation prefixes, peer survival and exact reclamation. Explicit divergences tested separately.
common.provenance: Join source candidates from audit_bif_batch.py; review full admitted upstream bodies and wrapper dependencies, retaining notices and source hashes. Candidate matches are not proof of executable semantics.

groups.contract: Native numeric identity/conversion/rounding/division over admitted integer and float representations, including signed zero and pinned boundary quirks. Preserve host floating environment; reject invalid numeric arguments as native errors. No host allocation outside accounting.

Native term predicates, boolean validation and exact sizes; preserve bitstring views and native term distinctions. Existing predicate instruction admission is not proof of an exported BIF binding. Verify guard failure versus body error.

Native base/options/number parsing and formatting, proper-list and character validation, native result/error precedence and locale-independent behavior. Reuse real conversion machinery and existing BEAM wrappers where appropriate. Charge input and output size without changing transport limits.

Native list/tuple/binary/iovec construction and traversal, including partial bits, range rules, improper inputs and overflow. Preserve aliasing/refcounts and root sources across allocation; no publication before validated construction.

Native character-list semantics over the owned atom namespace. Existing-only conversion never interns; new atoms require namespace/accounting transactions. Validate native length and codepoint boundaries and preserve errors before publication.

Native ETF sizing/encoding for admitted terms and reviewed options, not fabricated encoding. Share size/encode invariants, atom/function/identity rules and binary-view handling. Explicitly refuse unimplemented valid modes rather than silently ignoring options; account temporary and compression work if admitted.

Pure native packet parser over supplied bytes, with packet-type/options limits and exact incomplete/error/rest results. Does not open sockets or consume ambient input. Preserve returned subbinary ownership and charge scans.

Native MD5 contexts and term hashing/range rules, including exact representation/equality subtleties. Context input is untrusted and must be parsed safely. No cryptographic-security claim; deterministic reference vectors, incremental equivalence, malformed contexts and charged traversal.

Return/remove actual process dictionary entries and exact-value key matches. Materialize results before destructive publication; keep key/value roots and code leases correct. Empty results only for genuinely empty/no-match state.

Real fun application/metadata/formatting and external-fun construction with native argument and arity semantics. Retain code through GC and owner teardown. Missing executable targets do not create fabricated exports; review intrinsic apply dispatch separately from preloaded stubs.

Native guest exception/exit behavior and stacktrace/catch semantics. These are not capability denials. Implement required correct unwind and compare ordinary caught errors against uncatchable capability failures.

Actual owned-process GC, reduction/scheduling and hibernation behavior on the single Engine worker. Never grant extra invocation work, fabricate a GC success, or add a public external suspend/resume lifecycle. Preserve live arguments, continuation/code roots and wakeup semantics.

Owned alias/link/monitor state and native options/messages, cancellation/flush rules and process-death cleanup. Local process modes must work; explicitly unavailable remote/port/service modes fail at the host boundary. Prevent descendant capability failures becoming host success through DOWN handling.

Real local process creation, linking/monitoring/options and asynchronous request lifecycle, including local-node variants. Preserve validated BEAM wrappers and causal budgets. Remote-node creation is denied before creating proxies or distributing; do not deny valid local variants because their signatures also accept a node.

Actual owned names, PIDs/aliases and inbox delivery with native option/result semantics, charged copy/candidate work and real registration ownership. Queries use the current namespace; remote/host-port effects are unavailable. Preserve send instruction and dynamic exported forms.

Owned timer identities, monotonic deadlines, native options and actual timer delivery/cancellation races serialized on the worker. Retain message/code roots and causal ownership; reclaim cancelled/expired timers. No host callback may interpret guest code.

Real local process metadata, group leaders, flags, liveness and snapshots/iterators. Native validation/order and dead-process results; account snapshot storage and retain no dangling process pointers. Group leadership does not create an ambient I/O service. Unsupported selectors require explicit refusal, never invented values.

Native identity parsing/formatting and node extraction for admitted namespace identities, with canonical native bounds. Constructing a textual identity is not spawning a process or opening a port; existence checks remain separate. Do not introduce remote identities or alias peer namespaces.

Actual clocks and native calendar/unit conversion, with supported epoch/timezone/DST/range contracts stated explicitly. Preserve negative rounding and bignum overflow behavior. Do not fabricate deterministic timestamps or alter host clock/timezone configuration; reference tests separate nondeterministic observations from exact conversions.

Real owned uniqueness and monotonic/positive option semantics, overflow-safe and serialized. Document namespace scope and replacement behavior; preserve counter state on failed result construction according to native effect/publication rules.

Published code/catalog identity and actual scoped allocation/runtime statistics. Add real accounting instrumentation where necessary. Scope and supported selectors must be documented; no host-global ERTS statistics, invented categories, fake uptime or claimed full OTP version parity.

Reviewed meaningful Isolate-local flags change actual owned runtime behavior and return native previous values. Host/Engine-global mutations and unavailable selectors fail explicitly. A returned previous value without changing supported behavior is not implementation.

Native argument/options validation and accurate unnamed, disconnected namespace behavior: no peers and no configured distribution cookie. nodes(known) and nodes(this) include the owned local node; nodes/2 returns node/info-map pairs even with an empty options map, with this-node connection_id undefined and node_type this when requested. Invalid filters/options are badarg. With no distribution service, disconnect_node returns ignored even for non-atom arguments; do not invent a badarg or false result. get_cookie returns nocookie from the unconfigured owned distribution state.

Real port-free state and native validation/dead-port query behavior; no invented live-port metadata or data. Type/selector/error precedence follows reviewed native sources. No query implicitly opens a port or accesses a host descriptor.

Pure native match-spec behavior and meaningful owned-process tracing/query state for explicitly admitted modes. Trace events must derive from actual execution and stay inside the Isolate; account compilation, matching and messages. Host tracer/NIF/distributed targets remain unavailable, and unsupported selectors are explicit. No fake successful trace activation.

Adapt the actual no-USE_VM_PROBES branches of pinned bif.c: spread accepts only booleans and returns true; restore accepts only true and returns true. Other inputs raise badarg. This is native disabled-probe behavior, not a generic successful stub or permission to enable host probes. The opcode manifest explicitly selects USE_VM_PROBES=0. Installed OTP 28/ERTS 16.3 instead demonstrated the enabled branch (spread returns {0,[]}; restore(true) is badarg), so those reference results are a documented configuration difference, not the oracle for the disabled branch.

Explicit host capability failure for runtime code preparation/installation/lifecycle or guest NIF execution. No hidden loader state, code replacement, on_load execution, library opening or namespace mutation. Denial remains distinct from unresolved imports.

Explicit host capability failure before stdout/stderr output, host termination, port/driver operations or process-display effects. Do not close descriptors, launch programs or return fabricated success. Test malformed arguments too: whole-MFA denial does not execute upstream effectful wrappers.

Explicit host capability failure before enabling/configuring distribution, node monitors or distribution-controller traffic. No peers, authentication service or node naming is synthesized to satisfy the binding.

Require an atom module and a binary code argument (bit length divisible by eight, including unaligned binary views); wrong types are badarg after entry charge. Look up actual published state with charged traversal. If present, return {module,Module} without inspecting/installing supplied bytes or changing code/exports/on_load. If absent, host capability failure. Result allocation can still fail; test unchanged code identity and arbitrary binary payloads.
